title: Elections, Oil, and Neocloud Stocks, Oh My!
summary:
Elections, Oil, and Neocloud Stocks, Oh My! 

             
             
            There are 3 publicly traded neocloud stocks that are big enough to care about. All 3 hit new long term lows today (ranging from 6 months to over a year).  All 3 continue to track very well with the recent bond market rally. This is simplest way to approach today's gains. The more you wander from that path, the more complex and circular the logic becomes. Oil prices have plummeted almost $20since last Friday. Seems like it should matter, and a few traders might agree. Then there's the election, which caused a surge in the broader stock market. We'd be careful giving it credit for bond market gains considering yields jumped from 4.90% to almost 4.95% when the senate results were called by news agencies. The easiest way to attempt to connect those dots would be via "AI company headwind implications." Such headwinds could imply slower corporate bond issuance or even a slower pace of economic growth. Bottom line: we have no objection to the lowest rates in more than a month, but the rally still looks most dependent on neocloud jitters.

title: Mortgage Rates Fall Back Under 7.25%
summary:
30yr fixed rates moved over 7.25% on September 23rd, 2026 and continued to long-term highs of 7.61% by early October. But starting in mid October, rates began declining as the market grew increasingly concerned about the tech sector. Until today 7.27% marked the floor of the present rally. Now the floor is lower.  Rates began the day moderately lower with an average top-tier 30yr fixed rate of 7.25%. Reasons can be debated, but may include:  
 Investors coming off the sidelines after mid-term election uncertainty was cleared up 
 Ongoing trouble for the neocloud portion of the tech sector (i.e. Coreweave, Nebius, etc) 
 Another sharp drop in fuel prices  
  Earlier in the day, it wasn't a given that rates would end up lower. Just after 10am, it looked like the stock market might get so much love that bonds/rates would be left wanting. But tech stocks ended up hitting their ceiling for the day at that time and bonds were subsequently able to improve to their best levels in the afternoon.  When bonds improve enough intraday, mortgage lenders occasionally adjust rates lower. Not every lender did so today, but it would enough to bring the average down to 7.22%--the first time we've been below 7.25% since September 22nd.   [thirtyyearmortgagerates]

title: AI Strategy, SaaS, HELOC, Non-QM Products; Webinars; Capital Markets React to Election Results
summary: Yes, there was/is an election which is certainly a discussion topic here in Dallas, but regardless of the results, many people who don’t own homes want to buy one, and people who do may be facing life changes and could use personal advice. Here’s a trend: Homeowners who won’t give up a 3 percent mortgage are becoming landlords instead. Do you have a product (and underwriting) to help them at every stage? Another reason for personal consulting with borrowers: A fixed-rate mortgage may remain stable for thirty years, but the cost of owning that home does not. Property taxes continue to rise, insurance premiums are increasing across much of the country, utility costs are climbing, and climate-related risks are beginning to reshape both local markets and the availability of coverage. Those expenses are becoming a larger driver of affordability than interest rates alone, yet they remain secondary considerations in many lending, servicing, and valuation models. The result is a growing disconnect between qualifying someone to purchase a home and preparing them to successfully own it over the long term. Homeownership should not be evaluated solely at origination, but rather over the full life of the loan. (Today’s podcast can be found here. This week’s ‘casts are presented by FirstClose, which helps financial institutions grow a successful home equity business with innovative solutions that minimize application drop-off, automate time-consuming processes, and reduce time to close from weeks to days. Today’s has an interview with FirstClose’s John Aslanian on home equity lending trends and how their platform aims to improve lenders’ efficiency and borrower experience.)

title: Volatile Gains as Markets Digest Elections and Data
summary: There are several moving parts to today's trading levels, but the TL;DR is that bonds are holding modest gains so far despite some 2-way volatility. The overnight session started out with the strongest gains of the day, clearly coinciding with a stock market swoon.  Stock prices and bond yields bounced higher when the senate majority was called around 11:30pm ET. Bonds quickly unwound most of the overnight gains before stabilizing sideways at slightly stronger levels. Stocks have been rising ever since. In other words, there was no magical relief in the bond market about political gridlock or the defusing of the risk of $5k payouts (who knows if that would have happened, but if it did, it would have implied more Treasury borrowing). Stocks saw additional gains at the open. This put some pressure on bonds. Then at 10am, the ISM data led to another small bout of selling as the comments reflect forward-looking inflation concerns.

summary: Home contract signings fell 17% year over year in October, reaching their lowest level for the month on record, as higher mortgage rates continued to squeeze buyers out of the purchase market, according to Realtor.com's latest housing report.The annual decline was the steepest since March 2023 and marked the fourth consecutive month of falling contract signings.
